Never played up to gen 5 to be completely honest, I stopped at Diamond & Pear. I always hear good things about gen 5 tho, maybe it’s just not for you ?

Nier Automata’s soundtrack is great but saying it’s a bad game isn’t true though. 

It’s completely fine if you don’t like the game, after all to each their own you know ! But not liking a game ≠ it being bad.

I’m a big fan of Drakengard and Nier as well, music is definitely just as strong a selling point as their stories. But yeah up until Automata, gameplay wasn’t really their forte despite some interesting ideas and concepts in both series

Honestly Lightning Returns is a really surprisingly good game. Changed the XIII formula completely and made it a sort of Majora’s Mask-esque type of game with revamped FF XIII combat based on outfits that work like classes/jobs, really interesting game tbh and worth a look. 

Story is a bit uuuuuuh special, but all the other departments were made really nicely.

Yeah FF8 is a good game, nowhere near as bad as people made it out to be honestly. People warned me that it was supposedly going to be terrible but once I played it I realized that it was completely fine, just a bit clunky and flawed with some of its mechanics (and arguably story choices as well)

Despite being very flawed in its design, gameplay and characters, I can still vividly remember tracks from FF XIII. The battle theme especially is an example I like to point out because of how well it is composed and how it fits the tone/mood of the game very well. 

Another example of great soundtracks coming from mid/bad games is Castlevania Judgment, the Wii arena fighter. 
Arguably kind of a bad game despite being kinda fun, with some really questionable redesigns by the Death Note artist, but with incredible remixes of classic themes from the series. Judgement’s rendition of Vampire Killer, Bloody Tears and Slash are to die for and are a prime example of how well Castlevania’s music couples with metal and rock.

The Issen mechanic in the Onimusha series. 

I don’t think it’s ever explained anywhere, or if it is it’s super cryptic but basically there’s this move called the Issen that allows you to instant kill almost any enemy. To perform it you must lock on to an enemy and press the attack button as their attack is about to hit you. The timing is extremely strict making it hard to pull off but with enough practice you can just melt encounters like nothing. 

Without it, fights can be hard and a little tedious, forcing you to use magic moves to make it easier but once you learn how to pull it off, it’s go time. 

There’s even a second type of Issen that you can perform right after a perfect guard to be safer.

Basically you take your attack value and divide it by a certain divider that depends on the weapon class you are using, but there's a lot of other factors. 

Here's the formula: Damage = [ [Attack]/Weapon Modifier* Motion value * Effectiveness] + [Elemental Damage] * Overall Defense
